steps.text: There are always chimes like little bells resounding from the dome, the result of countless tentacle-shaped bio-monitors analyzing the most minute changes in the ocean current.
Occasional dull roars echo faintly from the port, as warships coming to and from the harbor gracefully displace vast amounts of seawater, like gigantic fins.
The goods, flying through aerial optic cables in squeezed state to every household, emit a near-subsonic buzzing.
These myriad noises, varied yet not chaotic, have become the ambiance of Milliarium, long since faded into the background for its ten thousand or so residents.
But now, all those residents stop in their paces. They wonder if their ears are deceiving them.
At first, it was like a wisp of wind sweeping across an angular reef.
Then, like a newborn who tentatively poked its head out of the warm womb.
And after that, a colony. A nest. An entire region of sea.
The thick, bizarre sound of blooming of life could be heard clearly.
The children of the sea now give back to the ocean.
They give civilization a kiss, and civilization is now filled to the brim with life.

steps.name: Tense Ægir
steps.text: Look!
The usual tower looming over the city center is gone, replaced by an enormous stone column, the type seen only in karst caves in the sea.
Layer upon layer of fine, porous, slimy, and smooth Seaborn tissue encircle the walls of the beacon tower.
Yet light from the equipment within still permeates, casting an ethereally enchanting glow over its surroundings.
Microbial colonies float down from the column, blossoming into oddly-shaped lifeforms.

steps.name: Tense Ægir
steps.text: If it weren't for the statues I can just barely make out, I'd have thought these were untouched wilds!

steps.name: Mysterious Ægir
steps.text: ...'Nest conversion.'

steps.name: Tense Ægir
steps.text: Why would there be Seaborn in the city? I know we haven't—

steps.name: Mysterious Ægir
steps.text: Doesn't matter if we did or not, as long as the results are as expected.

steps.name: Mysterious Ægir
steps.text: I just hope it's a lesson those ever-sinking Ægir will never forget.

steps.name: Tense Ægir
steps.text: What do we do now?

steps.name: Mysterious Ægir
steps.text: We keep it growing, and stop the city from pushing it back.
Was murdering Tullia not enough? Do you need to destroy the entire city to sate your appetite for chaos?
At first, I was planning to tail you back to your allies and save myself some effort.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: But since it's an emergency, I'll have to haul my net in now.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: You will be the thirty-third and thirty-fourth Church of the Deep's cultists caught by the Sea Patrol this month.

steps.name: Tense Ægir
steps.text: The Sea Patrol...

steps.name: Mysterious Ægir
steps.text: You've harmed a lot of our brothers and sisters lately.

steps.name: Mysterious Ægir
steps.text: Clinging to the current order will do you no good. What Ægir needs isn't a struggle for its life in despair, it's—

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Shut up. I'm not here to debate.

steps.name: Sea Patrol Captain
steps.text: Praefecta Secunda, an unusual concentration of bio-signatures has been detected. They've tripled in number in a short time.

steps.name: Sea Patrol Captain
steps.text: It seems the Seaborn have fully converted the tower into their nest, and are now steadily producing more of themselves.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: We cannot allow them to spread to the other city units!

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: The nearby civilians have already started evacuating by themselves. Take a squad to guide them to the emergency shelters.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Remember to clear the roads of all support machines. If the Seaborn contaminate them, they could be used as weapons against us.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: The rest of you, get in formation and deploy barriers. Keep the Seaborn within the perimeter of the beacon tower!

steps.name: Sea Patrol Captain
steps.text: Yes, ma'am!

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: I was sure the Class IV weapons had already been activated. Don't tell me...

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: ...I'm listening.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Lock down all Class IV weapons immediately. I want a thorough inspection of the entire system, as soon as possible.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: All troops who have fallen back, regroup at the port immediately.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: From now on, all combatants are to remain on standby on the channel.

options: This isn't quite what you described.
I'm guessing this isn't part of the plan?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Look at this real-time nautical chart. Just an hour ago, Seaborn bio-signatures were generally stable.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But now, every nest on the continental shelf is getting closer and closer to each other... No, it's not that the nests are moving. They are expanding endlessly.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Like countless drops of ink spreading across a sheet of paper.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: This entire stretch of sea is turning into a nest.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The scattered nests are linking together as one, with Milliarium in the middle.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Did Ægir really bring weapons to disperse them, Madame Consul, or a mass of catalysts? Are you annihilating them, or feeding them?

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: If Blandus tampered with the link between the beacons and the weapons, it must have been him who altered their effect as well.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: And as a result...

options: Ægir's hopes of landfall have been exploited.
The city's now a foothold for Seaborn expansion.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: As the Waterway Program's Chief Designer of Warfare, I will take full responsibility for this. But we haven't lost the battle quite yet.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Look outside. Not a hint of disturbance on the streets. Milliarium has not yet sunk into panic.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: We've struggled against the Seaborn for more than two hundred years. We've experienced countless incidents like this. It's far too early to declare Milliarium 'lost to the enemy.'

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Dr. Kal'tsit, Doctor, you must leave the city at once. I'll escort you to the port.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I had assumed a consul would need to remain at her post.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: As things stand, the port is the heart of the city. A key military installation we cannot afford to lose.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: The Seaborn have already invaded my city. You think I'll wait for our uninvited guests to knock on the Pensivarium's door?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Gah—

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: The air's getting more humid the further we go. I-I can barely breathe...

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Watch your step. Use your device to float over. Don't step on that.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: ...Nethersea Brand?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Indeed. Yet another means for the Seaborn to extend their reach. They've already spread from the top of the tower to here, much faster than you'd see on land.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: The Seaborn are nesting in the city?!

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Above our very heads.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: You said there was someone directing them... Why? How?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: This is the work of that dead man, Blandus. He spent the last five years on this.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: According to his farcical plans, the signals emitted by this tower would, along with the weapons we brought, become a bridge connecting humanity and the Seaborn.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: He has indeed built a 'bridge' of sorts, but the Seaborn have not reciprocated his ambitious goodwill.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Our connection has only served to alert the beasts to Milliarium's position, and given them an understanding of our defense mechanisms.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: The Legions had taken great pains to divide this stretch of sea into manageable regions, but with the nests now converging on the signal, they are whole once more.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: The Class IV weapons that should have destroyed the nests and repelled the Seaborn have done the exact opposite. Seaborn tissues grow along their firing paths. What should have withered was instead nourished.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Hmph. Even until death, he never realized his own arrogance.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Señor Ulpianus, I don't quite understand what you're saying. But right now...

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: The Seaborn already consider this tower a new nest. It will steadily spawn and attract more from other nests to gather here.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Can we reverse the change?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: It's too late.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: We have only one option. Eject the city unit the beacon tower stands on.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: ...Eject?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: But underwater cities aren't built in blocks. How would you—

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: There is still much you do not understand about Ægir.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Unlike the nomadic cities of the land, pieced together from cumbersome plates, Ægir technology focuses on the biological, especially when it comes to city construction.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Biting off a poisoned limb is an instinctual reaction in a seabeast. Nothing difficult.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: We must keep the remainder of the city, for it still has use. Otherwise, the Seaborn in the area will eventually unite into one, and no one would ever be able to stop them then.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: They'll come ashore without a hint of resistance. They'll land in... Iberia...

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: What do we have to do exactly?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: A massive yet precise framework supports each city unit of Milliarium. The operation system controlling the linkage of the tower's unit should be in this control center.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Once activated, it will send the entire tower into the depths.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: ...Is this it?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I can operate it—but there's no response.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: It doesn't seem like there's any issue with the system, so it must be the linkage itself...

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: The Institute of Facility Management has specialists dedicated to the maintenance of the framework. It is less likely to malfunction than a Hunter's weapon is to rust.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: And yet, here we are. Precisely at a time like this...

steps.name: 'Little Handy' from Institute of Facility Management
steps.text: Reading error occurred (2).

steps.name: 'Little Handy' from Institute of Facility Management
steps.text: Run fault diagnostics?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Do you need my help, Mr. Avitus?

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Oh, no. I was merely observing this abandoned Little Handy.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Could he...

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Could he know something about this?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I might know who to look for.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Contact the Ægir soldiers outside. They'll help you exit this place.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Are you going to stay here? Alone?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: You still have doubts about me, young one. Good.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: But someone needs to stay in this control center.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Once the tower completes its conversion, Milliarium will be unable to eject it, even if we manage to repair the linkage.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: A seabeast cannot spit out its heart, when the heart is no longer its own.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: I must remain to confirm that the framework has resumed operation, then eject the tower myself.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: But if you do that, you'll sink along with it... into the hordes of Seaborn...

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: You needn't worry about that. Or do you mean to say you'd be more suited for that duty?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: You don't have much time, young one.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Y-You have already—
Isn't this the frequency of the beacon tower?
Secunda, Sea Patrol. Who's inside the tower?

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Then what about Blandus?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: He's dead.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: The two of us were in contact, but I never noticed anything unusual. I should submit myself to the consul for discipline once this is settled.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Milliarium must abandon the tower. I must see it sink into the abyss with my own eyes.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: And after that?

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Will you return to Ægir? Can you return to Ægir?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: I told you not to ask pointless questions, Secunda.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: You should not allow the past to render you indecisive.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: ...You're overthinking things.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Blandus told me what happened back then.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: As far as I'm concerned, it doesn't matter which of you rejected my application.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Though I'm willing to admit that... I regret not becoming a Hunter and fighting alongside you all. Deeply.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: I'll admit that I felt anger and resentment for a long time. I even envied Skadi.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: But eventually, I became accustomed to patrol work. For your sake. For the sake of the project keeping our home, our civilization, safe.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Staying outside of a specific project will allow you to see more sacrifices, more betrayals, more untrustworthy people, more things deviating from their paths.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Like you, right now?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Have you thought through what you should bear?

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: If you truly did betray Ægir, if you really are associated with that scum, then you're in that tower now to plan your escape. I'd bear the guilt of allowing a fallen Ægir to flee.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: If you're still a Hunter, then you'll be fighting alone. However, it's already impossible to wipe your slate clean after infiltrating the city, breaking into the tower... not to mention the outcome of the tribunal.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Ægir may not remember your sacrifice... Just like how Tullia will inevitably be forgotten.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: But I agree. Ejecting the tower is the most effective way to help Milliarium respond to this disaster.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: I approve of your choice. I'll afford you some limited amount of trust.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Hmph. Very well.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: You have five minutes. After that, I'll come rescue that land dweller in the tower.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: The entire city is following the emergency transportation coordination plan. We'll enter the axial channel via the Sophontheatrum and leave for the port.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: I will remain there to direct operations, while the Sea Patrol takes command of this ship and sees you to dry land.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: The drone matrix will also head to the lighthouse and assist Iberia in mounting a defense.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Should the city not organize an evacuation of its citizens as well?

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Milliarium is a military fortress. It is able to accommodate its citizens during battle. All civilians have already been escorted to shelter by the Sea Patrol.

options: Those neural cables by your hand...
Should they be... twitching like that?

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: No. With communications down, my connection to the ship's operating system has also been cut off... I'm losing control.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Little Handy, run diagnostics on the entire ship.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: The systems breach is more serious than I expected.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: We might not have enough time to land. I'm sorry.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: At least the city's artificial gravity is still functional. The devices you have will help you move freely through the air.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Now follow me. No need to be scared; all you have to do is walk out the door.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Comms are still down. Looks like someone managed to cut off the entire Sophontheatrum from the outside.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: —Mon3tr!

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: (Vigilant screech)
Mon3tr spreads its ebon talons as a wave of heat washes over you. At nearly the same time, the consul draws her ceremonial sword and steps to the side to cover you and Kal'tsit.
You take a good look at the 'enemy' before you.
An unusually-shaped Seaborn bars your way.
It seems to lack hostility. Before Mon3tr's roar startled it, it simply stood there quietly, its featureless face illuminated by the coral-shaped terminal in the middle of the Sophontheatrum.
The granular organelles surrounding its body spread out like arms, 'stroking' the branches of the terminal, and fusing with the flowing characters and symbols on it.
Was it observing? Sensing? Can it even comprehend human perception and reasoning?
It turns towards you.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: A... Seaborn. Is it the one that breached the terminal? This is unprecedented. And not a good sign.

steps.name: Mysterious Seaborn
steps.text: (Garbled Ægirian) There is no justice here. Only the path ahead.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: A Seaborn trespassing in an Ægirian city, reciting an ancient proverb in a sanctum designed by sages past.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: This might be the most ironic scene I've witnessed since I joined this war. Uncouth, even for a provocation.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Its use of language and its manner of speaking... are all unlike the usual outcome of the Seaborn's forced 'learning.'

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I fear this Seaborn was once human, Madame Consul.

steps.name: Mysterious Seaborn
steps.text: Language. Never have I forgotten it. Never has it abandoned me.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: What about your thoughts? Do you actually comprehend yourself when you clumsily mimick the sayings of the wise?

steps.name: Mysterious Seaborn
steps.text: Comprehend? No. I did not understand their true meaning, even as I left them for posterity.

steps.name: Mysterious Seaborn
steps.text: Now, I have a new understanding.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Left for posterity... Mártus?

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: You're Mártus?!

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: The key member of the fourth observation team of the mantle ruins, the scholar of anthropology and prehistoric civilization who went missing more than two centuries ago? That Mártus?

spans.text: The key member of the fourth observation team of the mantle ruins, the scholar of anthropology and prehistoric civilization who went missing more than two centuries ago?

steps.name: Mysterious Seaborn
steps.text: ...In my most distant memories, I was once, known by that name.

steps.name: Mysterious Seaborn
steps.text: But now, you need only be cognizant of my appearance. You see before you a Seaborn. Call me as such.

steps.name: Mysterious Seaborn
steps.text: 'Seaborn.'
The Seaborn floats towards you.
Through its transparent skull, you see strangely colored orbs gather and disperse, steadily changing their formation.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: Ægir. Allow me to converse with the one behind you.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: (Angry howl)

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: Glub—Tell your little friend to stow its fangs. Its flames cannot burn my blood.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: AMa-10—

options: Who are you? Why did you call Kal'tsit that?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Stay vigilant, Dr. {@nickname}. I'll speak with it.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: Kal-tsit... Kal'tsit. I see now. If you are accustomed to that name, I can call you by that.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: I have waited for you, Kal'tsit, for the two of you, for a very long time.
